title: Understanding Linearly Separable Data
text: A dataset is linearly separable if there exists a linear boundary that can perfectly separate the data points of different classes. This means that a straight line (in 2D) or a hyperplane (in higher dimensions) can be drawn to separate the classes without any misclassification.

title: Logistic Regression on Linearly Separable Data
text: Logistic regression is a linear classifier. If the data is linearly separable, logistic regression can find a decision boundary that perfectly separates the classes, achieving 100% accuracy on the training data.

title: Overfitting Concerns
text: While logistic regression can achieve 100% accuracy on a linearly separable dataset, it may not generalize well to new, unseen data. This is because the model might overfit the training data.

title: Evaluating the Statement
text: Given that logistic regression can perfectly separate linearly separable data, is it possible to find a classifier that achieves 100% accuracy on such a dataset?
